*sets down coffee, removes glasses, rubs eyes*

Listen to me. I've seen a lot of code disasters come across my desk, but this one? This is the kind of thing that ends up on the front page of the Post. "It works in staging." You know what else worked in staging? The Hindenburg worked in staging.

Let me walk you through what I found.

---

## Critical Issues

**SQL Injection - Multiple Locations (Lines 97, 111-114, 128, 151-153, 183-185, 197-199)**

Every single one of these string-formatted queries is a wide open door. `GetOrder`, `GetUserOrders`, `CancelOrder`, `ExportOrders` - an attacker could drop your entire database or extract every credit card you've ever stored. This alone is enough to kill this PR.

**Credit Cards Stored in Plain Text (Lines 79, 199)**

You're storing raw credit card numbers in your database and then *exposing them in a CSV export*. This is a PCI-DSS violation that will get you fined into oblivion. The "masking" on line 204 will panic on empty strings too.

**Payment Processed Before Order Saved (Lines 56-67, 78-85)**

You charge the customer, *then* try to save the order. If the database insert fails? You've taken their money with no record. That's called theft where I come from.

---

## High Severity

**No Authentication or Authorization**

Anyone can cancel any order. Anyone can export all credit cards. Anyone can bulk update prices. What's next?

**Race Condition in Cache (Lines 86, 95-99)**

You're writing to the cache without holding the mutex. That's a data race waiting to corrupt your cache.

**Goroutine Closure Bug (Lines 136-141)**

Classic Go mistake - `productID` and `quantity` are captured by reference in that loop. Every goroutine will use the *last* iteration's values.

**Ignored Errors Everywhere**

Lines 43, 51, 57, 63, 71, 111, 128, 172... you're ignoring errors from HTTP calls, JSON decoding, database operations. When these fail - and they will - you'll have no idea why.

---

## Medium Severity

**No Timeouts on HTTP Calls (Lines 51-55, 57-60, 70-74)**

External services hang? Your whole service hangs. Use `context.WithTimeout`.

**Response Body Never Closed (Lines 51, 60, 67)**

Memory leak. Every request leaks a connection.

**Float64 for Money (Lines 27, 47)**

Use integer cents or `decimal`. Float arithmetic will give you off-by-one-cent errors that'll drive your accountants insane.

**No Input Validation**

Negative quantities? Negative prices? Zero items? All accepted happily.

---

## The Fix

This needs to go back to development. Parameterize every query. Encrypt or tokenize cards. Add transactions around payment+order creation. Add authentication. Add timeouts and proper error handling. Fix the goroutine closures.

I've been down in this hole before. I know the way out. But it's not by merging broken code to main.

This PR is rejected.
